title: GEMのカスタム指示が『長くする』や『再試行』ボタンで無視される現象の修正要望
body:
普段創作などで便利に利用させていただいています。

GEM（カスタムGemini）で一人称や視点（視点・特定の語尾など）を細かく指定して利用しているのですが、スマホアプリ版で回答生成後に『長くする』や『再試行』ボタンを押すと、GEMの指示（Instructions）が無視され、一人称や語り手の視点が勝手に切り替わってしまう現象が多発しています。

Web版（ブラウザ版）ではこのような指定の無視は起きにくいため、アプリ版の修正ボタン（再生成・テキスト編集アルゴリズム）の処理において、カスタム指示の優先度が下がってしまう仕様・不具合があるように見受けられます。

せっかくの便利なボタン機能ですので、アプリ版でもGEMの設定（カスタム指示）が最後までしっかり反映されるよう、アップデートでの改善を強く希望します。

title: DNPs
body:
I’m writing this review so other customers don’t go through what I just experienced.

I placed multiple sports combo positions involving the same player. That player was identified as OUT and ultimately did not participate in the game at all. Yet his player props were still available to trade.

I assumed that if a player never participated, those player-specific props would be voided or the money associated with those affected positions would be returned. That is NOT how Kalshi handles it.

Kalshi uses something called a scalar settlement. Their DNP description, in my opinion, is far too vague considering how severe the financial consequences can be. Customer support explained scalar settlement to me using an example where a market trading at 70% would settle at $0.70 instead of $1.00 or $0.00. That sounds relatively straightforward when discussing ONE market.

What wasn’t obvious to me was what happens when multiple DNP props are inside the same combo.

On one of my 3-leg combos, Kalshi assigned the affected components settlement values of $0.37, $0.22 and $0.84. Those aren’t simply averaged or treated as one DNP event. They are multiplied together:

0.37 × 0.22 × 0.84 = approximately $0.068 per contract.

On another position involving four props tied to the same player, I put in $499.88. After the player did not participate, I received only $38.31 back.

That’s a $461.56 loss — 92.34% of my position — involving a player who never stepped on the field.

That’s the part I believe customers need to understand before putting their money into these markets.

My issue isn’t simply that I lost money. Losing is part of taking positions on sports. My issue is that I don’t believe the potential consequences of Kalshi’s DNP/scalar settlement system are communicated clearly enough to an average customer.

If multiple props involving the same player are scalar-settled, multiplying those partial values together can absolutely destroy the value of the entire combo. Reading that a market may receive a “scalar settlement” does not intuitively tell a customer:

“THIS PLAYER CAN NEVER PARTICIPATE AND YOU CAN STILL LOSE MOST OF THE MONEY YOU PUT INTO THIS COMBO.”

And there’s another question Kalshi needs to address: If a player has already officially been identified as OUT, why are customers still able to purchase player-specific props involving that player?

At minimum, once a player is confirmed OUT, Kalshi should either stop accepting new positions on that player’s props or display an unavoidable warning directly before purchase explaining exactly what will happen.

Something as simple as:

“WARNING: This player is currently listed OUT. If the player does not participate, your position WILL NOT automatically be refunded. A scalar settlement may apply. In combos containing multiple affected components, those settlement values may be MULTIPLIED together and you could lose a substantial portion of your investment despite the player never participating.”

That would have completely changed my decision.

Kalshi customer support told me that simply returning everyone’s original investment wouldn’t account for traders who made profitable trades before the cancellation/DNP and that scalar settlement is intended to preserve that market value. I understand that reasoning for an individual market.

But that explanation does not adequately address what happened to my multi-leg combo.

Multiple props involving the same player were affected by the same underlying event—the player not participating—and the scalar values compounded against each other.

I’m not claiming customers should never lose money. I’m saying customers deserve to understand exactly how much risk a DNP creates before they click purchase, especially when Kalshi already has information showing that the player is OUT.

I learned this lesson by watching approximately $500 turn into $38.

If you’re considering using Kalshi for sports player props, please read their DNP and scalar-settlement rules very carefully. Do NOT assume that a player being OUT or never participating means your position will be voided or your money returned.

I hope Kalshi changes how this is communicated so another customer doesn’t have to learn this the expensive way

body:
I find myself using this quite a bit to search for things. While the Ai isn’t always totally accurate, which is to be expected, it is often very helpful. Sometimes I’ll find myself googling something like a potential side effect of a medication with an antibiotic, next thing I find out that simply eating a banana each day will help with the side effect of feeling ‘down’ the second week of my antibiotic treatment. Ai taught me that and it’s right too! It works and I am grateful for this information, it’s saving me. 

Most of the time I google records or songs, lyrics, movies, actors, etc., and not only are the regular search results exactly what I’m looking for, most of the time the Ai part is where I go and it does take feedback and accept if you tell it that it’s wrong about something. It’ll correct itself and apologize for the incorrect information. That’s helpful and polite, as well as a bit terrifying that it’s capable of learning like that. 

All in all, it’s a helpful app that I use all of the time. Probably daily. 👍🏻

title: Won’t let me withdraw balance from selling
body:
I sold around $50 worth of clothes on Depop, and I will give them credit for the ease of selling and the visibility Depop gives your listings. 
However, every time I try to add my bank account to withdraw my balance, I receive a message that says “an unknown error has occurred” with no elaboration. I tried to reach out to support and was met with an AI chat bot. The bot couldn’t help me resolve the issue, so it said that someone from support would email me within 72 hours. Over a week later, and I have heard absolutely nothing. I even emailed support myself today with no reply. Depop also has no phone number for support, so if they choose not to reach out to you you’re just out of luck. I still have not received any help and am completely unable to withdraw my balance. The balance also can’t be used to purchase other items on Depop, so I went through the effort of selling my clothing, Depop collected fees from the sales, and I receive nothing.
Also, do not be mislead by the “No selling fees” claim that they advertise. Depop does collect fees from the buyer and the seller for sales, the fee is just listed sneakily under a little “I” information button and listed as a service fee instead of a selling fee.
All in all, I am extremely disappointed with Depop, especially in their support department.

title: Work
body:
Feature request: Link chats and projects to share code context.

I had two separate projects in different Claude chats, both using the same backend server. When building the second application, I needed to add new functionality to the server code that originated in the first project. But the chat couldn't directly see the code or context of the other chat. I had to manually ask one Claude instance to write out a prompt describing the changes, then paste that prompt into the other chat so it could update its own copy of the code.

Suggestion: add the ability to link chats or projects together, so Claude can directly access the code and context of a related chat and propose consistent changes across both, especially useful when multiple applications share a common backend server, without the user having to manually relay information between chats.

body:

For anyone who spends time outdoors or needs to track natural light for photography, this app is indispensable. Highly recommended.
